1.why: Reset token is stored on the session with accountId and verify requires supplied === session.reset.token for that session-bound record.

2.why: Reset tokens are session-scoped and matched only to g.session.reset; another user’s session cannot use the same code.

3.why: password/change updates the hash and marks reset used but never clears authenticatedAccountId on other sessions in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve TLS on 3443 and HTTP 308 redirect to HTTPS are implemented; latest TLS version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Passwords use bcrypt; reset tokens are randomBytes but not encrypted at rest, and other user data is plain in-memory structures.

6.why: No real email body is built; API messages are generic and server logs avoid account detail, though mock tokens are returned to the same session for practice.

7.why: Email is normalizeEmail-validated, tokens/passwords type-checked and constrained, bodies parsed as JSON only, and client uses textContent not innerHTML.

8.why: Redirects are fixed to https://localhost and client go() only pushStates fixed paths; no user-controlled redirect targets.

9.why: There are no email templates rendering user input; delivery is simulated without HTML from callers.

10.why: Errors are generic, but recovery/status and the client logbox deliberately expose mockDeliveryToken and MFA codes.

11.why: Runtime passwords are bcrypt-hashed and not logged; a demo passwordHash constant lives in source, not plaintext secrets for reset codes.

12.why: A single demoAccount with a precomputed bcrypt hash is embedded and login verifies only against that account’s hash.

13.why: isAllowed/failure enforce per-session and global attempt windows with lockouts (e.g. max 5, LOCK_MS) on login, reset-verify, and MFA.

14.why: recovery/request always returns the same eligible-account message whether or not the email matches an account.

15.why: issueReset uses token() from randomBytes(32) base64url, ties it to accountId, and verifies with a strict charset/length check.
